about: Rows produced by running pfb_unbound.py (CPython 3.11) over the inputs described in pfb_unbound_abp_test.go

lines.in: ! Title: ADR-07 representative ABP DNS sample (trimmed, hand-curated)
! This is a syntactic exemplar set, not a verbatim feed.
! --- plain ||domain^ blocks (the only class today's lite parser keeps) ---
! --- @@ exceptions (dropped today -> the over-blocking the ADR fixes) ---
! --- hosts-style lines (AdGuardHome accepts these in adblock feeds) ---
! --- IP-anchored / hosts-IP (PHP firewall path; Python returns None) ---
! --- regex rules: see regex_reducible.txt / regex_irreducible.txt for the bulk;
!     a couple inline here so the sample alone exercises the dispatch ---
! --- element-hiding / cosmetic (DNS-only scope SKIPS all of these) ---
! --- path / URL rules (not a whole-domain DNS decision -> SKIP) ---
! underscore label (#723): DNS-legal, accepted by production and the oracle alike
! ADR-07 regex patterns that SHOULD fold to a domain/wildcard rule at build time
! (zero added per-query cost). Each line: a /re/ (block) or @@/re/ (allow) whose
! anchored grammar reduces to exact-domain (data) or wildcard-subtree (zone).
! --- plain fully-anchored, no metachars in body (still reducible) ---
! --- @@ allow forms that reduce to a whiteDB entry ---
! ADR-07 regex patterns that stay REAL compiled patterns (cannot fold to a
! domain/wildcard). These become per-query cost; the spike measures the inline
! scan latency at feed scale and the ReDoS exposure on a <=253-char input.
! --- finite char-class / quantified label bodies (NOT expanded by design) ---
! --- substring / unanchored (matches anywhere in the name) ---
!     Real feeds rarely ship these, but the safety layer must handle them; the
!     spike times their worst real first-hit on a <=253-char crafted input.
!     NOTE: the nested-quantifier body is anchored to a fixed literal domain
!     (redos-exemplar.example) rather than a bare \w+ catch-all -- a bare \w+$
!     tail matches EVERY dotted probe (any domain name), which silently masked
!     the corpus-wide reconcile-vs-oracle equivalence test (issue #718). Still
!     a quantified group the admission gate refuses (`pfb_regex_admission` reports
!     "quantified group" on the inner `(\w+\.)+`); it just no longer swallows unrelated
